configuration_map: All four points A, C, B, D are collinear in the order A—C—B—D. C is given as an arbitrary interior point of AB. D is constructed on the extension of AB beyond B with BD = BC. The entire proof operates on this single line with no off-line auxiliary points, no angles, no triangles, and no circles. After the geometric setup in Steps 1-2, the proof is purely algebraic: applying identity 2.4 to AD cut at B, applying identity 2.7 to AB cut at C, and combining the results through algebraic manipulation (adding equals to equals, substitution).
pass_reason: All spatial claims concern collinear points in the order A-C-B-D, which are mutually consistent. The proof is essentially algebraic after a minimal geometric setup, combining two Book 2 identities (2.4 and 2.7) through algebraic manipulation. No angle decompositions, no interior/exterior claims, no circle arguments — nothing that could produce a spatial configuration contradiction.
